text:
**Short answer:** Panasonic Eneloop Pro is the best all-around pick. Standard Eneloop or IKEA LADDA are better if you want longevity or a low price.

| Need | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Best overall / high-drain (cameras, flashes, controllers) | **Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA** | 2550 mAh, keeps about 85% charge after 1 year, rated for about 500 recharges. Digital Camera World calls it its most reliable. The guide listed it around $21.89 for a 4-pack. [Buying options](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) |
| Longest life / everyday use | **Panasonic Eneloop AA (standard)** | 2000 mAh, rated for about 2,100 recharges, keeps 70% charge after 10 years of storage. [Buying options](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) |
| Cheap and good | **IKEA LADDA AA 1900 mAh** | $9.99 for 4 at IKEA US. Charge-Test measured it close to its rating and says the line is Eneloop-class. [Buy at IKEA](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/) |
| Bulk and high capacity | **Tenergy Premium PRO AA 2800 mAh** | $42.99 for 20 ($11.99 for 4). The maker claims 85% charge after 1 year and 1,200 cycles. [Buy from Tenergy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack) |
| Devices that need 1.5V | **EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA** | Matches alkaline voltage, unlike the 1.2V NiMH cells above. [Buying options](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) |

**Caveats**
- **Affiliate link:** the Tenergy link is an affiliate link from Dealectric. Its figures are manufacturer claims, not independent tests.
- **LADDA 2450 mAh:** reviewers say it's the Eneloop Pro equivalent at about half the price ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/), [GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)). The US page I found lists only the 1900 mAh version, so I couldn't confirm US stock or price for the 2450.
- **Frame & Focal tests:** I wouldn't lean on these articles ([one](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-gives-you-the-best-bang-for-your-buck), [two](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-best-after-one-year-abuse-440920)). Their numbers conflict with each other and with other sources, and they describe zinc dendrites in NiMH cells, which doesn't make sense.
- **Voltage:** NiMH cells are 1.2V. A few devices built strictly for 1.5V alkalines may show them as low.
- **Charger:** you'll need a decent charger. IKEA sells the STENKOL for $8.99. Most NiMH cells ship partly or fully pre-charged.

I can narrow this down if you tell me what devices you're powering and whether you need a charger.
